title: Nine Pieces in the Pocket
subtitle: 货币与零钱 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 货币与零钱（社会服务与人际沟通·货币与消费）
meta: 主题语境：货币与零钱（社会服务与人际沟通·货币与消费）　|　核心词汇：cent　|　正文 334 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 cent 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1955 my mother was sent to count ① cent she could not spend, and she said the counting was the whole of the lesson. The ② cent, meaning the coin and not the sum, was nine pieces and was counted by whoever came last; cent, she said, is the only thing in a pocket that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ cent in that pocket had the same edge, and the ④ cent at the end, meaning the one the shopkeeper kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever counted properly. Cent, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ cent was the whole of the wage, meaning the value it carried and not the coin. The ⑥ cent, meaning the value and not any of that, is the only thing in a wage that everybody counts and nobody questions; cent, he said, is either something you count or the only word that means both a coin and a value. She said the value is the part they remember.

By 1968 the ⑦ cent had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the edge. The ⑧ cent of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine pieces and eleven years of counting; cent, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ cent I remember is the one at the end, which was counted in 1973 and is still described as the brightest in the county. A ⑩ cent, my grandmother said in 1978, is the only thing that improves by being counted; every cent, she said, is a value that has agreed to look like a coin. She said the value was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 分币（指那枚硬币本身，与那笔钱相对）
C. 固定搭配：count a cent 数一分钱
D. n. 分币（指口袋里每一枚）
E. n. 分币（指末尾那一枚）
F. n. 价值（抽象：它承载的那点价值）
G. n. 那点价值（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The cent, meaning the coin and not the sum
cent was the whole of the wage
the cent had become a number in a report
The cent of the whole thing
A cent, my grandmother said in 1978

answers.why: count a cent 意为“数一分钱”，1955 年母亲被派去数她花不出去的那几分钱。
cent 意为“分、一分硬币”，指那枚硬币本身而不是那笔钱，共九枚，由最后来的人点数。
cent 指口袋里每一枚分币，每一枚都是同样的边。
cent 指末尾那一枚（店主留下的那一枚），是唯一有人认真点数过的。
cent 意为“价值”，抽象指它承载的那点价值，父亲说 cent 就是那份工资的全部。
cent 为抽象用法，指那点价值本身，是一份工资里人人都数、却没人质疑的东西。
cent 意为“分、一分硬币”，到 1968 年这枚 cent 成了报告里的一个数字。
cent 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九枚硬币和十一年的点数。
cent 意为“分币”，我记得的是末尾那一枚，1973 年数过，至今仍被说成全县最亮的。
cent 为抽象总称，祖母说一枚分币是唯一会因为被认真点数而变好的东西。
